title: 立场句
goal: 能用直接、明确且不改变问题范围的句子表达立场，并识别未回答问题的开头。
exam: TOEFL iBT（2026 年 1 月起的新版）· 写作

points.label: 写出直接回答问题的立场句
判断一个句子是否回答了问题

sources.title: ETS：TOEFL iBT Test 2026 Update — Test Blueprint and Specifications

body.p: 立场句回答教授要判断的那件事。第一句可以表示支持、反对或有条件支持。只说话题重要，或只说双方都有道理，都没有作出决定。

body.box:
Question: Should a city keep its public swimming pools open in winter?
Position: I favor winter opening at pools with enough local demand.

body.p: 这句保留了要判断的 winter opening，并用 enough local demand 限定支持的条件。改写题目时可以换句型，但判断的对象不变。冬季开放不能写成全年免费。

cards.title: 立场句的形式
rows: 直接支持
写明支持的做法，不必加 I think。
The city should keep its pools open in winter.
直接反对
否定所问政策，不否定整个话题。
I oppose requiring every pool to open in winter.
有条件支持
支持的决定和条件写在同一句里。
I support winter opening provided that demand covers staffing needs.
有限支持
只支持其中一部分对象，并写明是哪一部分。
Winter opening makes sense for pools used by local teams.
比较选择
从题目给的方案中选一个，再说明取舍。
Keeping one pool open is preferable to shortening hours at every pool.
同意同学
写出同意的具体主张，不只写 I agree。
I agree with Mei that the city should retain a winter swimming service.

cards.title: 问题范围与改写
rows: 只介绍背景
Public pools provide exercise.
未决定冬季是否开放：Pools should remain open in winter.
重复题目
Should pools open in winter? This is the question.
未作判断：Winter access should be maintained.
笼统同意
I agree with both students.
未说明取舍：I favor opening only the busiest pool.
空泛条件
It depends on the situation.
条件不明：I support opening if staff can be retained.
偷换对象
All winter sports should be free.
免费和所有运动都超出了问题：Winter pool access is worth retaining.
保留关键词
I favor winter access to public pools.
pool 这类关键词可以重复，不必每个词都换。

body.box:
Professor: Should university clubs elect leaders annually or let them serve until graduation?
Writer's view: Annual elections are preferable because members need a regular chance to change leaders.
Draft: Club leadership is important, and both arrangements have advantages.

Which opening expresses the writer's view?
1. Club leaders should serve until graduation to preserve stability.
2. Members should choose their club leaders again each year.
3. Club leadership matters under either election arrangement.
4. Graduation is an appropriate time to reconsider club activities.

body.p: 第二项把 annual elections 改写成 choose ... again each year，直接选定了一个方案。第三项接近草稿，仍然没有选择。第一项与作者的立场相反，第四项把领导任期换成了活动安排。
立场句不必包含全部论证。Members need a regular chance to change leaders 可以放在下一句，作为理由。

groups.text:
Professor: Should a college charge separately for optional field excursions?
Writer's view: Separate payment is acceptable only if a no-cost alternative fulfills the same course requirement.

items.stem: Which opening preserves the writer's condition?
options: Optional excursions should always be included in tuition.
Separate fees are acceptable when a free equivalent is available.
A free alternative should be offered only to students who pay.
Separate fees are preferable because alternatives are optional.
items.why: only if a no-cost alternative fulfills the same course requirement 对应 when a free equivalent is available，条件不能删去或倒置。

groups.text:
Professor: Should a town replace printed bus timetables with electronic displays?
Draft: Electronic displays and printed timetables both provide travel information.

items.stem: Why does the draft fail as a position sentence?
options: It favors printed timetables without explaining their cost.
It favors displays without considering printed information.
It describes a shared function without choosing a replacement policy.
It rejects travel information instead of comparing its formats.
items.why: both provide travel information 只是共同功能，没有回答 replace ... with 是否合适。

groups.text:
Professor: Should students select their own debate topics?
Writer's view: Topic selection should remain with instructors to ensure enough shared preparation material.

items.stem: Which opening directly states that view?
options: Instructors should continue to decide which topics students debate.
Students should select topics after instructors prepare shared material.
Debate topics should depend entirely on students' interests.
Shared preparation matters more than who chooses debate topics.
items.why: selection should remain with instructors 对应 instructors should continue to decide，不能改成学生选题。

groups.text:
Professor: Should a city prioritize repairing old playgrounds over constructing new ones?
Draft: Playgrounds deserve public investment.

items.stem: What decision is missing from this opening?
options: Whether public investment in playgrounds should increase each year
Whether playgrounds serve a public purpose
Whether new playgrounds need public funding
Whether repairs should take priority over new construction
items.why: 题目中的 prioritize repairing ... over constructing 要求排列优先级；deserve public investment 未作这种比较。

groups.text:
Professor: Should science courses require students to keep paper notebooks?
Writer's view: Students should choose the format; a paper requirement is unnecessary.

items.stem: Which opening expresses opposition to the requirement?
options: Paper notebooks should be required for all scientific observations.
Courses should allow students to choose how to record their work.
Students should use paper whenever their observations are important.
Students should choose the format of their paper notebooks.
items.why: Students should choose the format 对应第二项的 choose how to record，反对的是强制用纸质形式。第四项沿用了 choose the format，但仍然要用纸质笔记本。

groups.text:
Professor: Should a community choir hold auditions or accept all applicants?
Draft: I favor accepting everyone who applies, even if some need additional practice.

items.stem: Which assessment of this opening is accurate?
options: It avoids choosing between the two admission policies.
It makes acceptance depend on passing an audition.
It chooses open admission while acknowledging varied preparation.
It recommends excluding applicants who need further practice.
items.why: accepting everyone who applies 明确选择开放录取；even if some need additional practice 不构成筛选条件。

items.stem: The professor asks whether an art college should retain courses in traditional printmaking.
items.why: support 后接具体决定 the retention；that teach traditional printmaking 限定 courses，避免只评价艺术重要。

items.stem: The professor asks whether seminars should require assigned seating; the writer opposes the rule.
items.why: oppose the requirement 直接否定所问规定；that students sit in assigned seats 说明规定内容。

items.stem: The writer supports online access to a local council meeting only if a recording remains available afterward.
items.why: depends on 明确条件；a recording that residents can replay 对应会后可回看。

items.stem: A professor asks whether a certificate should require an internship; the draft only praises practical learning.
items.lead: The opening does not state whether
items.why: whether 后补出被遗漏的政策判断，a condition for certification 对应 require an internship。

groups.text:
Professor: Should universities replace commercial introductory textbooks with freely licensed editions?
Writer's view: Replacement is worthwhile only when the free edition covers the required material.
Draft: Textbook costs matter, and freely licensed books are widely discussed.

items.stem: Which first sentence accurately states the writer's view?
options: Free editions should replace commercial books regardless of coverage.
Commercial textbooks should remain because course coverage matters.
I support replacement when the free edition meets the course's needs.
Universities should discuss free editions before considering textbook costs.
items.why: only when the free edition covers the required material 对应 meets the course's needs，保留有条件支持。

items.stem: What is missing from the draft opening?
options: A mention of the financial issue affecting textbooks
A reference to the existence of freely licensed books
A statement that textbook selection is a topic of debate
A decision about replacement and the condition for it
items.why: Textbook costs matter 评价成本，widely discussed 描述背景；两者都没有决定是否替换。

groups.text:
Professor: Should graduating design students present their final work in a public exhibition or only to faculty?
Writer's view: Faculty-only assessment is preferable because unfinished prototypes may be misunderstood by public visitors.
Draft: Both exhibitions and faculty reviews can involve discussion of prototypes.

items.stem: Which opening directly states the intended preference?
options: Final design work should be reviewed by faculty without a public exhibition.
Public exhibitions should replace faculty review of final prototypes.
Students should exhibit prototypes publicly once faculty have discussed them.
Discussion of prototypes is valuable in public and faculty settings.
items.why: Faculty-only assessment is preferable 对应 reviewed by faculty without a public exhibition，即第一项。第三项仍让学生公开展出。

items.stem: Why is the draft opening incomplete as an answer?
options: It rejects exhibitions even though the writer favors public review.
It states a shared feature without choosing an assessment audience.
It compares finished designs instead of discussing prototypes.
It requires both review formats although the question permits only one.
items.why: Both ... can involve discussion 只指出共同特征，没有选择 only to faculty 或 public exhibition。

items.stem: The writer supports reserving a section of a public beach for swimmers.
items.why: I favor 后接 the reservation，of an area 指明对象，后面的限制保留专供游泳的立场。

items.stem: The writer opposes making all residents pay for an optional neighborhood newsletter.
items.why: a charge that applies to residents who do not subscribe 明确反对向未订阅者收费。

items.stem: A professor asks whether the campus should provide free umbrellas; the opening only describes frequent rain.
items.lead: The opening fails to answer whether
items.why: whether 后的政策判断是 should provide ... at no charge，描述降雨不能代替它。

items.stem: A professor asks whether class representatives should be elected; the draft only praises representation.
items.lead: The draft does not say whether
items.why: students should elect their class representatives 明确问题中的选择方式；赞扬代表制度不等于支持选举。
